description: Under the supervision of the office's Legislative Counsel, the Law Clerk will support the Congresswoman's legislative and oversight work by conducting legal and policy research, preparing for and staffing Judiciary Committee hearings and markups, developing vote recommendations, and helping to advance legislation. Law Clerks will draft legal memoranda, hearing scripts, policy memos, briefing materials, and other written products. This position is ideal for high-achieving law students, preferably 2Ls or 3Ls, with a strong interest in public law, policymaking, politics, congressional oversight, or government service. Law Clerks will have the opportunity to engage in serious, substantive work across a wide range of issue areas, including antitrust, administrative law, civil rights and civil liberties, criminal justice, government reform (i.e., anti-corruption), intellectual property, oversight, privacy, technology (e.g., artificial intelligence), and voting rights. The clerkship is unpaid but may be completed for academic credit. The application period for Fall 2026 Law Clerks is now open and will close on July 9th at 11:59 PM ET.

Strong interest in public law, policymaking, politics, congressional oversight, or government service

how_to_apply: Email the following materials to Jayapal.DCLawclerk@mail.house.gov: (1) resume, (2) cover letter, (3) list of three references with email addresses, and (4) unofficial undergraduate and graduate transcripts. Combine all application materials into a single PDF and use the subject line: "Law Clerk – FirstName LastName."

description: The Washington, D.C. Office of Representative Joe Morelle is now accepting applications for an internship during the 2026 Fall term.
